_comment2: Remove the _comment keys — JSON does not support comments natively.
_comment3: Available inputs: Clast_length, Clast_width, Ellipse_major_axis, Ellipse_minor_axis,
_comment4: Equivalent_diameter, Surface_area, Score, Orientation, and any other column
_comment5: present in the per-clast detection CSV.
_comment6: Safe functions: sqrt, log (natural), exp, sin, cos, atan2, abs, min, max, pow.

name: Clast_length_mm
description: Long-axis length converted from metres to millimetres. Identical to Clast_length but displayed in mm — useful when your report tables or axis labels prefer millimetres.

name: Phi_length
description: Wentworth phi scale: phi = -log2(D_mm), where D_mm is the long-axis length in millimetres. Positive values are finer than 1 mm; negative values are coarser. Uses the long axis (Clast_length) as the grain-size proxy.

name: Custom_elongation
description: Complementary-elongation index: 0 = perfectly round, approaching 1 = fully rod-like. Equivalent to 1 - Clast_elongation. Useful when you want elongation expressed as a deviation from a sphere rather than a ratio.

name: Submerged_grain_weight
description: Submerged weight of a spherical grain (rho_s = 2650 kg/m3, rho_w = 1000 kg/m3): W' = g*(rho_s - rho_w)*(pi/6)*D^3. Based on Equivalent_diameter as the diameter proxy. Demonstrates a multi-term expression.

name: Shields_excess_stress
description: Illustrative example: a fixed multiple (3x) of the critical Shields shear stress, representing a rough flood-peak excess-stress estimate. Replace 3.0 with your site-specific ratio. Requires Shields_critical_shear_stress to be present in the CSV (generated by the Rasterize tab).
